sc1_inventory.session_status_transitions: AuthProvider derives status as `user ? "authed" : restored ? "anon" : "restoring"`. It starts "restoring" on every hard load while one silent POST /auth/refresh redeems the httpOnly cookie, then settles ONCE — to "authed" (setUser and setRestored land in the same batch) or to "anon". Later transitions are sign-in and sign-out only. The access token lives in memory, so before the settle there is no Authorization header to send.
sc1_inventory.why_an_early_read_is_not_self_healing: apiRequest only retries a 401 when it USED a stored token (usedStoredToken = opts.token === undefined && getAccessToken() !== null). During the restore there is no stored token, so a 401 is final — and an optionalAuth endpoint does not 401 at all: it answers, as an anonymous visitor, and the effect never re-runs.

contract.settled: false only while the boot-time silent refresh is in flight. The effect guard.
contract.viewerId: the signed-in account id, or null
contract.viewerKey: "anon" | "authed:<id>" — the dependency-list value. It reads "anon" WHILE RESTORING on purpose: a server-rendered first page was fetched with no viewer, so it IS the anonymous answer, and keying it that way lets a visitor who settles anonymous keep the seed and issue no browser request at all.

sc2_the_seam.why_two_hooks: useSettledSession goes through useSession (throws outside an AuthProvider); useSettledOptionalSession mirrors useOptionalSession for the components that also render bare, where no viewer can ever arrive and delaying would hang the surface instead of guarding it.
sc2_the_seam.why_both_settled_and_viewerKey: settled alone never re-runs the read; viewerKey alone never fires for a visitor who settles anonymous (their key never changed). The exhaustive-deps lint rule enforces that a guard reading `settled` lists it.
sc2_the_seam.list_seam: lib/use-appending-list.ts gained ONE option, `viewer`, taking useSettledSession whole. It holds the first request until settled, joins viewerKey to the query signature, and pins `initialPage` to the ANONYMOUS key rather than the mount-time key — so arriving already signed in (a client-side navigation) still replaces the seed.
sc2_the_seam.tests: 10 for the hook, 6 for the list option, plus a 'does not fetch while restoring' / 'fetches once settled' pair for every fixed component

sc5_single_search_emit.what_was_wrong: one browser search wrote TWO query_log rows: the client's POST /search/events batch (the row that reaches the user's own history page — handleSearchEvents is the only ingest path that sets allow_history) and the routed search.submitted core emits behind the same GET /videos/search
sc5_single_search_emit.correction_to_the_earlier_note: the A13 opt-out section attributed the routed row to 'the frontend's server-side fetch of GET /videos/search'. There is no such fetch: vidra-user server-renders /instance, the home feed and the watch video, and nothing else. The routed row landed anonymous because the BROWSER's own search request went out before the session had settled — the same defect this slice's SC1 closes — and because api.searchVideos sends no X-Vidra-Session either.
sc5_single_search_emit.mechanism: a client that emits its own search.submitted declares it on the request: X-Vidra-Search-Events: client. Core skips its routed emit for that request only.
sc5_single_search_emit.why_the_client_must_be_the_one_to_say_so: nothing on the server distinguishes a browser (which will send the event) from an API consumer (which will not), and an API consumer must keep the routed emit — it is the ONLY record its searches ever leave. Accepting the caller's word is safe in the one direction that matters: the declaration can only make core collect LESS about that caller, and never touches anyone else's rows. An unrecognised value fails toward recording.
sc5_single_search_emit.contract: no OpenAPI change: the header follows X-Vidra-Session, the sibling client-supplied search header this contract also carries only in prose.

A muted author on a signed-in viewer's home page is still present in the server-rendered HTML for the moment before hydration. Measured as a fact, not fixed: the Next server cannot read vidra_refresh (Path=/api/v1/auth) and so cannot know there is a viewer.
findings_recorded_not_fixed: GET /me/notifications/unread-count is requested TWICE per page load, by NotificationsBell and by BottomTabBar independently. Both carry the bearer; it is a duplicate fetch, not a correctness bug.
GET /me/oauth-identities is requested twice on /settings, by ConnectedLogins and BlueskyVisibilityToggle.
GET /channels/{handle}/donation-addresses is requested twice on the watch page.
api.searchVideos sends no X-Vidra-Session, so before this slice the routed row it produced could not be correlated with the client's row for the same search even in principle.

The watch page's captions read can still go out unauthenticated when a public server seed paints first. Harmless (a public video's captions are public), but it is the one read left that fires before the settle.
